WHO recommends the use of calibrated drapes for direct estimation of postpartum blood loss compared to visual estimation after vaginal birth. 13. A study conducted across multiple countries in Europe assessed the effectiveness of calibrated drapes versus visual estimation for blood loss measurement. The evidence was of moderate certainty and deemed important. 14. Another study in India compared calibrated drapes with the gravimetric technique for blood loss estimation, with moderate certainty of evidence and important findings. 15. A study in China compared two-set liquid collection bags with visual estimation and calibrated blood collection bags, finding low-certainty evidence with critical importance. 16. The WHO emphasizes the importance of accurate postpartum blood loss assessment and the use of treatment bundles for postpartum hemorrhage management. 17. Various studies have highlighted the limitations of visual estimation of blood loss, with systematic reviews and randomized trials showing that objective methods like calibrated drapes or collection bags are more accurate. 18. The accuracy of blood loss estimation is critical for early detection and management of postpartum hemorrhage, as highlighted in multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses. 19. The cost-effectiveness of postpartum hemorrhage interventions, including early detection and treatment, has been analyzed in systematic reviews, with mixed findings depending on the context and resources available. 20. The introduction of quantitative blood loss assessment methods has been associated with changes in clinical practice and improved outcomes in observational studies. 21. WHO and other global health organizations continue to advocate for improved methods of blood loss estimation and management to reduce maternal mortality and morbidity worldwide.
